newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks end largely firmer, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks end largely firmer, seen up.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks traded largely firmer in an active market on Wednesday with brokers and analysts saying they were likely to continue strong if money market rates ease further on the back of a sharp drop in annual inflation.
The key 57-share industrial index rose 51.18 points to close at 8,080.71, prompted up largely by blue-chip beverages and hotel conglomerate Delta's 35-cent gain to 3,400.

"There's potential of the shares going up if the tender rate falls tomorrow (Thursday) at the weekly auction and we could see the stock market getting liquidity from the money market," one broker said.

"But generally, the market perception is the inflation figure is too low," he added, referring to Central Statistical Office figures on Wednesday which showed that Zimbabwe's year-on-year consumer price inflation fell to a seven-year low of 13.9 percent in November from 20.2 percent in October.
Some economic analysts said the fall was largely due to a drop in fruit and vegetable prices but others were sceptical that these prices could have weighed so heavily on the inflation basket.

"The (inflation figure) will put further downward pressure on the already depressed short-term money market, which can only be very positive to the market," said stock and money market analysts Dataworld.
On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Wednesday, construction firm J and F rose 50 cents to 250, Alloys in reasonable turnover gained 25 cents to 800 as did tobacco company TSL to 650.
Transport group Clan, pork processor Colcom and engineering firm Gullivers each added 10 cents to 350, 340 and 250 respectively.
Against the trend, packaging group Hunyani and local conglomerate TA Holdings each lost five cents to 350 and 155 respectively.
In minings, Falgold put on five cents to 110 while Wankie Colliery in reasonable turnover traded 20 cents up at 450. Nickel producer Bindura, however, dropped 50 cents in reasonable turnover to 850.
The seven-counter mining index shed 14.13 points to 1,096.61.
